newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Cemig says May 6 sale of stake delayed.
newsitem.headline: Cemig says May 6 sale of stake delayed.

text.p: The planned May 6 sale of a 32.9 percent stake in Brazilian state power utility Cemig has been delayed because companies pre-qualified for the auction asked for more time to visit the firm, a Cemig spokeswoman said.

The spokeswoman told Reuters that firms now have until Wednesday to visit Cemig and a new date for the National Development Bank's planned sale of 18.7 million debentures convertible to a 32.9-percent stake in Cemig will be set afterward.
"After Wednesday, a new auction date will be scheduled," she added.
Officials at the bank, known as BNDES, were not available to confirm the auction had been delayed.

Five firms -- Southern Electric Brasil Participacoes Ltda, Community Energy Alternatives Americas Inc., Pacific Generation Development Co., Copel, and a consortium of Artica Investment Group and CEA group -- have pre-qualified for the auction.
Cemig is owned by Minas Gerais state but the stake being sold was transferred to the BNDES late last year to cover a 430 million-real state debt.
A base price of 60.37 reais ($57.03) per debenture was set and the sale is to take place on the Rio de Janeiro Stock Exchange.
